none_means: No qualifying prior reference verified; not a proof of novelty.

results.references:
- Jeremy Bernstein, Yu-Xiang Wang, Kamyar Azizzadenesheli, and Animashree Anandkumar. [signSGD: Compressed Optimisation for Non-Convex Problems](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v80/bernstein18a.html). 2018. Complexity: $O(B(1+\Delta/(\eta\varepsilon)))$ stochastic-gradient calls for minibatch signSGD when $\eta L_\Sigma/2+2S_\Sigma/\sqrt B\le\varepsilon/2$, where $\eta>0$ is the step size, $B\ge1$ is the integer batch size, $L_\Sigma=\sum_i L_i$ sums the diagonal quadratic-majorant coefficients, and $S_\Sigma=\sum_i\sigma_i$ sums uniform coordinate noise standard-deviation bounds.
- Hongyi Tao, Dingzhi Yu, and Lijun Zhang. [When and Why SignSGD Outperforms SGD: A Theoretical Study Based on ℓ₁-norm Lower Bounds](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.06615v1). 2026, arXiv preprint v1. Complexity: $O((1+L\Delta/\varepsilon^2)(1+\|\boldsymbol\sigma\|_1^2/\varepsilon^2))$ stochastic-gradient calls for minibatch SignSGD and a uniformly sampled iterate, where $\sigma_i$ uniformly bounds the noise standard deviation in coordinate $i$.

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: The objective is differentiable on all of ℝᵈ and may be nonconvex. It has finite infimum f⋆ and satisfies f(x₀) − f⋆ ≤ Δ. The infimum need not be attained.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: Each call at x returns the full vector g(x,ω) with mean ∇f(x). Calls use fresh i.i.d. seeds, including repeated calls at the same point. The public input gives d, the measurable seed space Ω, x₀, L > 0, S ≥ 0, Δ ≥ 0, and ε > 0. The objective, oracle map, sampling law, and infimum are hidden.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SeparableNoiseLinfSmooth.lean, Params and spec.publicInput, spec.valid, spec.Query, spec.Reply, spec.admissible. LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean, IID

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: Writing σᵢ(x) = (E|gᵢ(x,ω) − ∇ᵢf(x)|²)¹ᐟ², the bound is supₓ ∑ᵢ σᵢ(x) ≤ S. The coordinate noise profile can vary with x, and coordinates within one reply may be dependent.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SeparableNoiseLinfSmooth.lean, spec.admissible coordinate second-moment integrability and sum-of-square-roots bound

distinctive_assumptions.label: non_euclidean_geometry
distinctive_assumptions.details: The gradient satisfies ‖∇f(x) − ∇f(y)‖₁ ≤ L‖x − y‖∞ globally. The same dual ℓ₁ norm measures stationarity.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: Queries, gradient replies, and outputs belong to ℝᵈ with public finite dimension d.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm
accuracy.details: Return one measurable point X with integrable ‖∇f(X)‖₁. The criterion uses the first power of the full gradient’s ℓ₁ norm.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: E‖∇f(X)‖₁ ≤ ε under the product law of the algorithm seed and the oracle seed sequence, subject to the fixed oracle-call budget.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The setup pairs ℓ∞-to-ℓ₁ smoothness and expected ℓ₁ stationarity with a pointwise budget on the sum of coordinate noise standard deviations. That budget allows the noisy coordinates to change with the query point.
